about.title: Personal Injury Help in Dublin, California
about.longDescription: Dublin sits at a busy crossroads in Alameda County, and its growth has brought steady traffic to corridors like Dublin Boulevard, Dougherty Road, Amador Valley Boulevard, and Tassajara Road. In the most recent recorded year, the city logged 153 injury collisions and 197 people injured, along with 2 traffic deaths — numbers that reflect a community of nearly 58,000 residents moving through a network of arterial roads every day. Reports show crashes tend to cluster on Tuesdays between 5 and 7 p.m., a pattern likely tied to evening commute volume. Whether the injury happened in a car accident, a pedestrian incident, or a slip-and-fall, the aftermath is often confusing — medical bills pile up while questions about fault and insurance linger. Our team handles personal injury claims for people in Dublin and throughout Alameda County. We're not a middleman service; we work on contingency, meaning there's no cost unless we recover money for you.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: You Generally Have Two Years
items.desc: California law gives most injury victims two years from the date of the incident to file a claim. If a government entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're found partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in standard injury cases.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Unless We Win
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost and no fee unless we recover compensation on your behalf.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an injury in Dublin?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of the incident to file a personal injury claim. If your injury involved a government entity or vehicle, that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes six months, so it's wise to act promptly.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Dublin?
items.answer: Public crash records show higher collision counts along corridors such as Dublin Boulevard, Dougherty Road, Amador Valley Boulevard, and Tassajara Road, with reports often peaking on Tuesdays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are simply recorded patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility. Your recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Will I owe anything upfront for legal representation?
items.answer: No. We work on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost and we only get paid if we recover compensation for you.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In most standard personal injury cases in California, there is no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. The specific amount depends on the facts of your case, which our team can evaluate.
